ns4:Benchmark.ns4:title: Nutanix AOS STIG
ns4:Benchmark.ns4:description: DISA STIG compliance checks for Nutanix AOS (Acropolis Operating System).

ns4:Rule.ns4:title: Nutanix AOS must have DoD mode enabled.
ns4:Rule.ns4:description: <VulnDiscussion>DoD mode on Nutanix AOS enforces a comprehensive set of security hardening settings required for Department of Defense deployments. Without DoD mode enabled, the system may not meet the minimum security requirements for processing classified or sensitive information. DoD mode configures FIPS cryptography, strict session controls, and other security settings in a single operation.</VulnDiscussion><FalsePositives></FalsePositives><FalseNegatives></FalseNegatives><Documentable>false</Documentable><Mitigations></Mitigations><SeverityOverrideGuidance></SeverityOverrideGuidance><PotentialImpacts></PotentialImpacts><ThirdPartyTools></ThirdPartyTools><MitigationControl></MitigationControl><Responsibility></Responsibility><IAControls></IAControls>
ns4:Rule.ns4:fixtext:
Enable DoD mode on the Nutanix cluster by running the following command from a CVM: $ ncli cluster edit-params enable-dod-mode=true
Verify the setting with: $ ncli cluster get-params | grep -i dod

ns4:Rule.ns4:title: Nutanix AOS must limit concurrent sessions to 10 for all accounts.
ns4:Rule.ns4:description: <VulnDiscussion>Limiting the number of concurrent sessions per user is a countermeasure against denial of service attacks and resource exhaustion. Without session limits, an attacker who compromises credentials could open unlimited sessions to exhaust system resources or maintain persistent unauthorized access. Nutanix AOS must limit concurrent sessions to 10 per account to reduce this risk.</VulnDiscussion><FalsePositives></FalsePositives><FalseNegatives></FalseNegatives><Documentable>false</Documentable><Mitigations></Mitigations><SeverityOverrideGuidance></SeverityOverrideGuidance><PotentialImpacts></PotentialImpacts><ThirdPartyTools></ThirdPartyTools><MitigationControl></MitigationControl><Responsibility></Responsibility><IAControls></IAControls>
ns4:Rule.ns4:fixtext:
Configure the system to limit concurrent sessions by adding or modifying the following line in /etc/security/limits.conf: * hard maxlogins 10
Verify with: $ grep maxlogins /etc/security/limits.conf

ns4:Rule.ns4:title: Nutanix AOS must initiate a session lock after 15 minutes of inactivity.
ns4:Rule.ns4:description: <VulnDiscussion>A session lock is a temporary action taken when a user stops work and moves away from the immediate physical vicinity of the information system but does not want to log out because of the temporary nature of the absence. Requiring a session lock after 15 minutes of inactivity prevents unauthorized individuals from accessing an unattended management session. The session lock is implemented at the point where session activity can be determined via SSH ClientAliveInterval.</VulnDiscussion><FalsePositives></FalsePositives><FalseNegatives></FalseNegatives><Documentable>false</Documentable><Mitigations></Mitigations><SeverityOverrideGuidance></SeverityOverrideGuidance><PotentialImpacts></PotentialImpacts><ThirdPartyTools></ThirdPartyTools><MitigationControl></MitigationControl><Responsibility></Responsibility><IAControls></IAControls>
ns4:Rule.ns4:fixtext:
Configure SSH to terminate idle sessions by setting the ClientAliveInterval in /etc/ssh/sshd_config: ClientAliveInterval 900 ClientAliveCountMax 0
Restart the SSH service: $ sudo systemctl restart sshd

ns4:Rule.ns4:title: Nutanix AOS must display the DoD-approved banner before granting access.
ns4:Rule.ns4:description: <VulnDiscussion>Display of a standardized and approved use notification before granting access to the operating system ensures privacy and security notification verbiage used is consistent with applicable federal laws, Executive Orders, directives, policies, regulations, standards, and guidance. System use notifications are required only for access via login interfaces with human users and are not required when such human interfaces do not exist. The banner must be displayed prior to any login attempt to inform potential users of the legal implications of accessing the system.</VulnDiscussion><FalsePositives></FalsePositives><FalseNegatives></FalseNegatives><Documentable>false</Documentable><Mitigations></Mitigations><SeverityOverrideGuidance></SeverityOverrideGuidance><PotentialImpacts></PotentialImpacts><ThirdPartyTools></ThirdPartyTools><MitigationControl></MitigationControl><Responsibility></Responsibility><IAControls></IAControls>
ns4:Rule.ns4:fixtext:
Configure the system to display the Standard Mandatory DoD Notice and Consent Banner by editing /etc/issue to contain the approved text: "You are accessing a U.S. Government (USG) Information System (IS) that is provided for USG-authorized use only. By using this IS (which includes any device attached to this IS), you consent to the following conditions..."
Additionally configure the SSH banner in /etc/ssh/sshd_config: Banner /etc/issue

ns4:Rule.ns4:title: Nutanix AOS must implement FIPS 140-2 validated cryptographic modules.
ns4:Rule.ns4:description: <VulnDiscussion>Use of weak or untested encryption algorithms undermines the purposes of utilizing encryption to protect data. The operating system must implement cryptographic modules adhering to the higher standards approved by the federal government since this provides assurance they have been tested and validated. FIPS 140-2 validated cryptographic modules must be used on Nutanix AOS to ensure all cryptographic operations meet DoD requirements for protecting sensitive information at rest and in transit.</VulnDiscussion><FalsePositives></FalsePositives><FalseNegatives></FalseNegatives><Documentable>false</Documentable><Mitigations></Mitigations><SeverityOverrideGuidance></SeverityOverrideGuidance><PotentialImpacts></PotentialImpacts><ThirdPartyTools></ThirdPartyTools><MitigationControl></MitigationControl><Responsibility></Responsibility><IAControls></IAControls>
ns4:Rule.ns4:fixtext:
Enable FIPS mode on the Nutanix AOS system. This is typically enabled as part of DoD mode configuration: $ ncli cluster edit-params enable-dod-mode=true
To verify FIPS is active at the OS level: $ cat /proc/sys/crypto/fips_enabled The output should return "1".

ns4:Rule.ns4:title: Nutanix AOS must allocate audit record storage capacity to store at least one weeks worth of audit records.
ns4:Rule.ns4:description: <VulnDiscussion>In order to ensure operating systems have a sufficient storage capacity in which to write the audit logs, operating systems need to be able to allocate audit record storage capacity. The task of allocating audit record storage capacity is usually performed during initial installation of the operating system. Nutanix AOS must allocate enough audit record storage to retain at least one weeks worth of audit records to support after-the-fact investigation of security incidents.</VulnDiscussion><FalsePositives></FalsePositives><FalseNegatives></FalseNegatives><Documentable>false</Documentable><Mitigations></Mitigations><SeverityOverrideGuidance></SeverityOverrideGuidance><PotentialImpacts></PotentialImpacts><ThirdPartyTools></ThirdPartyTools><MitigationControl></MitigationControl><Responsibility></Responsibility><IAControls></IAControls>
ns4:Rule.ns4:fixtext:
Configure audit log storage by editing /etc/audit/auditd.conf and setting an appropriate max_log_file value: max_log_file = 50
Ensure num_logs is set high enough to retain one week of logs: num_logs = 10
Restart the auditd service: $ sudo systemctl restart auditd

ns4:Rule.ns4:title: Nutanix AOS must enforce password complexity by requiring at least one uppercase character.
ns4:Rule.ns4:description: <VulnDiscussion>Use of a complex password helps to increase the time and resources required to compromise the password. Password complexity, or strength, is a measure of the effectiveness of a password in resisting attempts at guessing and brute-force attacks. Password complexity is one factor of several that determines how long it takes to crack a password. The more complex the password, the greater the number of possible combinations that need to be tested. Requiring at least one uppercase character is one element of password complexity enforcement.</VulnDiscussion><FalsePositives></FalsePositives><FalseNegatives></FalseNegatives><Documentable>false</Documentable><Mitigations></Mitigations><SeverityOverrideGuidance></SeverityOverrideGuidance><PotentialImpacts></PotentialImpacts><ThirdPartyTools></ThirdPartyTools><MitigationControl></MitigationControl><Responsibility></Responsibility><IAControls></IAControls>
ns4:Rule.ns4:fixtext:
Configure password complexity by editing /etc/security/pwquality.conf and setting: ucredit = -1
This requires at least one uppercase character in all new passwords.

ns4:Rule.ns4:title: Nutanix AOS must enforce a minimum 15-character password length.
ns4:Rule.ns4:description: <VulnDiscussion>The shorter the password, the lower the number of possible combinations that need to be tested before the password is compromised. Password complexity, or strength, is a measure of the effectiveness of a password in resisting attempts at guessing and brute-force attacks. Password length is one factor of several that helps to determine strength and how long it takes to crack a password. Use of more characters in a password helps to increase exponentially the time and/or resources required to compromise the password. Nutanix AOS must enforce a minimum 15-character password length.</VulnDiscussion><FalsePositives></FalsePositives><FalseNegatives></FalseNegatives><Documentable>false</Documentable><Mitigations></Mitigations><SeverityOverrideGuidance></SeverityOverrideGuidance><PotentialImpacts></PotentialImpacts><ThirdPartyTools></ThirdPartyTools><MitigationControl></MitigationControl><Responsibility></Responsibility><IAControls></IAControls>
ns4:Rule.ns4:fixtext:
Configure the minimum password length by editing /etc/security/pwquality.conf and setting: minlen = 15
This enforces a minimum of 15 characters for all new passwords.

ns4:Rule.ns4:title: Nutanix AOS must use SSH protocol version 2.
ns4:Rule.ns4:description: <VulnDiscussion>SSHv1 contains known cryptographic weaknesses including susceptibility to man-in-the-middle attacks and session hijacking. If SSHv1 is used for remote management of Nutanix AOS, an attacker could intercept or modify administrative sessions, leading to full system compromise. All SSH connections must use protocol version 2 exclusively to ensure cryptographic integrity and authentication strength meet DoD requirements.</VulnDiscussion><FalsePositives></FalsePositives><FalseNegatives></FalseNegatives><Documentable>false</Documentable><Mitigations></Mitigations><SeverityOverrideGuidance></SeverityOverrideGuidance><PotentialImpacts></PotentialImpacts><ThirdPartyTools></ThirdPartyTools><MitigationControl></MitigationControl><Responsibility></Responsibility><IAControls></IAControls>
ns4:Rule.ns4:fixtext:
Ensure SSH is configured to use protocol version 2 only by verifying /etc/ssh/sshd_config contains: Protocol 2
Note: On modern versions of OpenSSH (7.4+), protocol 1 support is removed entirely. Verify the installed version supports only protocol 2.
Restart sshd after changes: $ sudo systemctl restart sshd

ns4:Rule.ns4:title: Nutanix AOS must synchronize time with an authoritative time source.
ns4:Rule.ns4:description: <VulnDiscussion>Inaccurate time stamps make it more difficult to correlate events and can lead to an inaccurate analysis. Determining the correct time a particular event occurred on a system is critical when conducting forensic analysis and investigating system events. Synchronizing internal information system clocks provides uniformity of time stamps for information systems with multiple system clocks and systems connected over a network. Nutanix AOS must be configured to synchronize with an authoritative DoD time source.</VulnDiscussion><FalsePositives></FalsePositives><FalseNegatives></FalseNegatives><Documentable>false</Documentable><Mitigations></Mitigations><SeverityOverrideGuidance></SeverityOverrideGuidance><PotentialImpacts></PotentialImpacts><ThirdPartyTools></ThirdPartyTools><MitigationControl></MitigationControl><Responsibility></Responsibility><IAControls></IAControls>
ns4:Rule.ns4:fixtext:
Configure NTP synchronization by editing /etc/chrony.conf and adding authoritative NTP servers: server ntp1.example.mil iburst server ntp2.example.mil iburst
Restart the chronyd service: $ sudo systemctl restart chronyd
Verify synchronization: $ chronyc sources

ns4:Rule.ns4:title: Nutanix AOS must alert designated personnel in the event of an audit processing failure.
ns4:Rule.ns4:description: <VulnDiscussion>It is critical for the appropriate personnel to be aware if a system is at risk of failing to process audit logs as required. Without this notification, the security personnel may be unaware of an impending failure of the audit capability and system operation may be adversely affected. Audit processing failures include software/hardware errors, failures in the audit capturing mechanisms, and audit storage capacity being reached or exceeded. Nutanix AOS must alert designated personnel in the event of an audit processing failure.</VulnDiscussion><FalsePositives></FalsePositives><FalseNegatives></FalseNegatives><Documentable>false</Documentable><Mitigations></Mitigations><SeverityOverrideGuidance></SeverityOverrideGuidance><PotentialImpacts></PotentialImpacts><ThirdPartyTools></ThirdPartyTools><MitigationControl></MitigationControl><Responsibility></Responsibility><IAControls></IAControls>
ns4:Rule.ns4:fixtext:
Configure auditd to take action when disk space is low by editing /etc/audit/auditd.conf: space_left_action = email action_mail_acct = root admin_space_left_action = halt
Restart auditd: $ sudo systemctl restart auditd

ns4:Rule.ns4:title: Nutanix AOS must enforce an account lockout after 3 consecutive invalid logon attempts.
ns4:Rule.ns4:description: <VulnDiscussion>By limiting the number of failed logon attempts, the risk of unauthorized system access via user password guessing, otherwise known as brute-force attacks, is reduced. Limits are imposed by locking the account after a specified number of consecutive failed attempts. Nutanix AOS must enforce automatic account lockout after no more than three consecutive invalid logon attempts to protect against brute-force attacks on management interfaces.</VulnDiscussion><FalsePositives></FalsePositives><FalseNegatives></FalseNegatives><Documentable>false</Documentable><Mitigations></Mitigations><SeverityOverrideGuidance></SeverityOverrideGuidance><PotentialImpacts></PotentialImpacts><ThirdPartyTools></ThirdPartyTools><MitigationControl></MitigationControl><Responsibility></Responsibility><IAControls></IAControls>
ns4:Rule.ns4:fixtext:
Configure account lockout by editing /etc/security/faillock.conf and setting: deny = 3 unlock_time = 900 fail_interval = 900
Ensure pam_faillock is properly configured in /etc/pam.d/system-auth and /etc/pam.d/password-auth.

ns4:Rule.ns4:title: Nutanix AOS must use TLS 1.2 or greater for all web management interfaces.
ns4:Rule.ns4:description: <VulnDiscussion>Transport Layer Security (TLS) encryption is a required security setting for ensuring data confidentiality and integrity over network connections to management interfaces. TLS versions prior to 1.2 have known cryptographic weaknesses (BEAST, POODLE, Lucky13) that allow attackers to decrypt or modify protected communications. Nutanix AOS web management interfaces including Prism Element and Prism Central must enforce TLS 1.2 as the minimum protocol version.</VulnDiscussion><FalsePositives></FalsePositives><FalseNegatives></FalseNegatives><Documentable>false</Documentable><Mitigations></Mitigations><SeverityOverrideGuidance></SeverityOverrideGuidance><PotentialImpacts></PotentialImpacts><ThirdPartyTools></ThirdPartyTools><MitigationControl></MitigationControl><Responsibility></Responsibility><IAControls></IAControls>
ns4:Rule.ns4:fixtext:
Configure the Nutanix cluster to enforce TLS 1.2 minimum: $ ncli cluster edit-params min-tls-version=TLS_1_2
Verify with: $ ncli cluster get-params | grep -i tls
For Prism Central, ensure the web server configuration enforces TLS 1.2 minimum.

ns4:Rule.ns4:title: Nutanix AOS must not use default SNMP community strings.
ns4:Rule.ns4:description: <VulnDiscussion>SNMP community strings are effectively passwords used to authenticate SNMP queries and traps. Default community strings such as "public" and "private" are well-known and documented in vendor manuals, making them trivial for attackers to exploit. If default SNMP community strings are not changed, an attacker can query the system for detailed configuration and network topology information, or potentially modify device settings via SNMP write access. Nutanix AOS must not use default SNMP community strings.</VulnDiscussion><FalsePositives></FalsePositives><FalseNegatives></FalseNegatives><Documentable>false</Documentable><Mitigations></Mitigations><SeverityOverrideGuidance></SeverityOverrideGuidance><PotentialImpacts></PotentialImpacts><ThirdPartyTools></ThirdPartyTools><MitigationControl></MitigationControl><Responsibility></Responsibility><IAControls></IAControls>
ns4:Rule.ns4:fixtext:
Remove or change default SNMP community strings by editing /etc/snmp/snmpd.conf. Remove any lines containing: rocommunity public rwcommunity private
Replace with organization-specific community strings or configure SNMPv3 with authentication: rouser snmpuser auth
Restart the SNMP service: $ sudo systemctl restart snmpd

ns4:Rule.ns4:title: Nutanix AOS must disable unnecessary services and daemons.
ns4:Rule.ns4:description: <VulnDiscussion>It is detrimental for operating systems to provide, or install by default, functionality exceeding requirements or mission objectives. These unnecessary capabilities or services are often overlooked and therefore may remain unsecured. They increase the attack surface of the system by providing additional vectors through which an attacker could penetrate. Removing or disabling unnecessary services reduces the attack surface and ensures that only required functionality is available on the Nutanix AOS platform.</VulnDiscussion><FalsePositives></FalsePositives><FalseNegatives></FalseNegatives><Documentable>false</Documentable><Mitigations></Mitigations><SeverityOverrideGuidance></SeverityOverrideGuidance><PotentialImpacts></PotentialImpacts><ThirdPartyTools></ThirdPartyTools><MitigationControl></MitigationControl><Responsibility></Responsibility><IAControls></IAControls>
ns4:Rule.ns4:fixtext:
Identify and disable unnecessary services. Common services that should be disabled on hardened Nutanix AOS systems include: $ sudo systemctl disable --now cups $ sudo systemctl disable --now avahi-daemon $ sudo systemctl disable --now bluetooth $ sudo systemctl disable --now rpcbind
Verify enabled services: $ systemctl list-unit-files --state=enabled --type=service
Only services required for Nutanix cluster operation should remain enabled.
